title: [task] 0.5.1 Analyze entity_types directory patterns
description: Document current entity type patterns in ai/entity_types/.

comments.author: Joshua Shin
comments.text:
ANALYSIS COMPLETE: Entity Types Directory Pattern Documentation

## Entity Types Structure Analysis

### Directory Location
`assets/scripts/ai/entity_types/`

### Current Entity Types (6 total)
1. **forager.lua** - Primary idle game creature
2. **lumberjack.lua** - Specialist idle game creature  
3. **kobold.lua** - Legacy combat creature
4. **gold_digger.lua** - Legacy resource creature
5. **healer.lua** - Legacy support creature
6. **demo_bot.lua** - Demo/testing creature

### Core Structure Pattern (Universal)
All entity types follow identical structure:
```lua
return {
    initial = { worldstate_atoms },
    goal = { default_goal_state }
}
```

### Three Distinct Patterns

#### Pattern 1: Idle Game Creatures (forager, lumberjack)
**Characteristics:**
- Comprehensive survival system (8-9 atoms)
- Resource sensing capabilities
- Work/behavior tracking

**Standard Atoms:**
```lua
initial = {
    -- Resource sensing (specialized per creature)
    nearTree = false,          -- forager + lumberjack
    nearRock = false,          -- forager only
    
    -- Survival system
    hungry = false,            -- hunger < 40
    starving = false,          -- hunger < 15 (urgent)
    hasFood = false,
    tired = false,             -- energy < 30
    exhausted = false,         -- energy < 10 (can't work)
    readyToReproduce = false,  -- hunger > 80 AND energy > 60
    
    -- Behavior tracking
    didWork = false,
    wander = false
}
```

#### Pattern 2: Legacy Combat/Resource Creatures (kobold, gold_digger, healer)
**Characteristics:**
- Simple combat-oriented state
- Starts hungry (hungry = true)
- Special ability flags

**Standard Atoms:**
```lua
initial = {
    hungry = true,             -- starts hungry
    enemyvisible = false,
    resourceAvailable = false,
    underAttack = false,
    -- Special abilities:
    candigforgold = true,      -- gold_digger only
    canhealother = true        -- healer only
}
```

#### Pattern 3: Demo/Testing Creatures (demo_bot)
**Characteristics:**
- Complex demonstration state
- Multiple behavior modes
- Well-documented goals

**Custom Atoms:**
```lua
initial = {
    patrolling = false,
    patrol_complete = false,
    threat_detected = false,
    alert_complete = false,
    tired = false,
    rested = true,
    idle = false
}
```

### Design Principles Observed

1. **Consistency**: All use same return structure
2. **Specialization**: Resource sensing varies by creature type
3. **Modularity**: Each creature defines only relevant atoms
4. **Documentation**: Comments explain purpose and thresholds
5. **Evolution**: Clear progression from legacy → idle game patterns

### Naming Conventions
- Files: lowercase, creature_name.lua
- Atoms: camelCase boolean flags
- Comments: Purpose and threshold documentation

### Integration Points
- Auto-loaded by ai/init.lua:36
- Used by goal_selectors/creature_name.lua
- Referenced in worldstate_updaters.lua for sensing

title: [task] 0.1.1 Identify UI layer lookup API
description: Research and document the exact API for acquiring UI layer handle for Screen space rendering.

comments.author: Joshua Shin
comments.text:
RESEARCH COMPLETE: UI Layer API Documentation

## Screen Space Rendering API (AUTHORITATIVE)

### Layer Acquisition
```cpp
// Get UI layer handle
auto ui_layer = GetLayer("ui");        // Named layer registry
auto sprites_layer = GetLayer("sprites");
auto bg_layer = GetLayer("background");
```

### Screen Space Rendering
```cpp
// Queue UI commands in Screen space
layer::QueueCommand<layer::CmdDrawRectangle>(
    ui_layer,
    [](layer::CmdDrawRectangle *cmd) {
        cmd->x = 100.f; cmd->y = 200.f;
        cmd->width = 300.f; cmd->height = 150.f;
        cmd->color = BLUE;
    },
    10,  // z-index
    layer::DrawCommandSpace::Screen  // Fixed to viewport
);
```

### Core Architecture
- **Layer Registry**: `s_layers` map with `GetLayer(name)`
- **Command Buffering**: Pool-based allocation, sorted by z-index
- **Render Spaces**: `DrawCommandSpace::Screen` vs `::World`
- **Built-in Layers**: "ui", "sprites", "background", "final"

### Lua Bindings
```lua
local ui_layer = GetLayer("ui")
command_buffer.queueDrawRectangle(ui_layer, init_fn, z, layer.DrawCommandSpace.Screen)
```

### Key Files
- `src/core/game.hpp`: Layer registry (`GetLayer`, `RegisterLayer`)
- `src/systems/layer/layer.hpp`: Core layer API
- `src/systems/layer/layer_command_buffer.hpp`: Command system
- `src/systems/layer/layer_lua_bindings.cpp`: Lua API

**RESULT**: Complete API documentation for UI layer acquisition and Screen space rendering
